clue.text: No 10, possibly, in revolt fiasco

parts.note: screws are sold by gauge number, and No 10 is one such size
people in revolt are up in arms, risen up

explanation.surface: Downing Street (No 10) rebelling turns into a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: No 10 suggests Downing Street, but here it is a screw's gauge number.
explanation.definitionFit: A botched job or mess-up is a fiasco, informal synonym.

clue.text: Crashing bores holding court, finally flash on and off

indicators.note: the scrambled letters hold the last letter inside
crashing suggests the bores are smashed into a new order
finally picks the closing letter of court

explanation.surface: Dull people who crash out while holding court make lights flicker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crashing' makes SROBE from BORES; T from court goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe light emits rapid flashes, so as a verb it means to flicker on and off.

clue.text: Cork, not for the first time, wraps drugs in material

definitions.text: Cork, not for the first time

indicators.note: the drugs are placed inside the material word

parts.note: real means material or physical
E is ecstasy, so Es is drugs plural

explanation.surface: A Cork dealer once again wraps drugs in fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork looks like the Irish city, but it is a verb meaning stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: To cork again is to stop a bottle a second time, a synonym of closing again.

clue.text: Kept open by the alert, brave investigator

parts.note: to brave a storm is to weather it
a private eye is an investigator

explanation.surface: An alert, courageous detective keeps watch.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'keep a weather eye open' means stay watchful, so it is what alert people keep open.

clue.text: The world's a small place — moving out

parts.note: PL is a short form of place

indicators.note: moving says the letters of out are shifted around

explanation.surface: The world feels tiny when you move house.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the saying 'it's a small world'; 'moving' rearranges OUT to UTO.
explanation.definitionFit: This dwarf planet is a distant world in the solar system.

clue.text: Music combination to depend on wearing underwear

indicators.note: the underwear is worn around the other piece, so it encloses it

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
to hang on something is to depend on it

explanation.surface: A musical combo relies on what its members wear underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combination' hints at another undergarment (combinations) but serves only as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhangra is a style of popular music from the Punjab, an example of music.

clue.text: Shakespearean character associated with drink and toast

parts.note: Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character is linked with drinking and toasting.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheer said before drinking is a toast, the drinker's call.

clue.text: Rockers possibly creamed off church melodies

indicators.note: creamed off means skimmed away, so letters are removed

parts.note: rocking chairs are an example of chairs

explanation.surface: Perhaps rock musicians skimmed tunes from a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rockers' suggests musicians, but means rocking chairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Airs are tunes or melodies, a synonym.

clue.text: Sort of dark grey with bluish sheen not encountered in western girl

definitions.text: Sort of dark grey with bluish sheen

indicators.note: the unmet word goes inside the girl word

parts.note: gal is a girl, American Western style
unmet means not encountered

explanation.surface: A cowgirl wears a grey dress no one has seen before.
explanation.definitionFit: This alloy's colour names a dull bluish-grey shade.

clue.text: City of Lincoln and river: a sort of Eden

parts.note: Abe Lincoln, US president

indicators.note: a sort of says the word Eden appears in a different form

explanation.surface: A city of Lincoln and its river is described as a kind of paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' rearranges EDEN to DEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish granite city in the north-east is an example of a city.

clue.text: Member of religion cut short god's thanks

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god, with the possessive S
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A believer briefly thanks a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a shortening of Rastafarian, an adherent of the Rastafari faith.

clue.text: Saying entire political party needs energy

parts.note: utter means complete or total
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's party
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A whole political party requires vigour to make its statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A saying or spoken remark is a synonym, both nouns for something said.

clue.text: Shelled sea creature getting round in chipboard buggy

indicators.note: the round letter sits inside the scrambled chipboard
buggy as an adjective means faulty, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A sea creature is wheeled around in a pushchair made of chipboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buggy' looks like a pushchair noun but signals the anagram of CHIPBOARD (BRACHIPOD), into which O goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamp shells are marine invertebrates with two hinged valves, an example of a shelled sea animal.

clue.text: Marshland inhabitant repulsed beast with club

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a deer is a beast
a mace is a spiked club

explanation.surface: Someone in the marshes drives off an animal with a cudgel.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulrush or cattail grows in marshes, so it is a plant that lives there.

clue.text: Cameron Isle is out of the Pacific island group

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: David Cameron departs from a Pacific archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Isle' looks like part of the place name but gives only I.
explanation.definitionFit: This collection of islands in the western Pacific is an island group.

clue.text: Injured thumb tops caught in secateurs somehow revive

indicators.note: the tops are trapped inside the other letters
somehow says the letters of secateurs are rearranged
the tops of the two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A gardener whose thumb is nipped by the pruners needs bringing round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' gives RESUSCATE; the thumb is injured in the gardening surface, but only the tops of those words matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone back to consciousness or life is to revive them, a synonym.

clue.text: Vet unexpectedly puts dog's name on bridle

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: Spot is a typical name for a dog
to bridle is to restrain or check

explanation.surface: A vet puts a bridle on a dog called Spot without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Vet looks like the animal doctor, but it is a verb meaning examine.
explanation.definitionFit: A random inspection without warning is vetting unexpectedly.

clue.text: Sparkling wine medium discovered in chopped peanuts

indicators.note: the medium is found inside the other letters
chopped means cut up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the clothing size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant turns up inside a bowl of crushed nuts with fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' rearranges PEANUTS into SPUANTE; M goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti spumante is an Italian fizzy wine, an example of sparkling wine.

clue.text: PanAm's top aircrew broken by commercial competition

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
broken says the letters of aircrew are shattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Pan Am's senior flight staff were broken by fierce market rivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitive undercutting of charges between firms is a form of commercial rivalry.

clue.text: Spoilsport legal person rotten about exercise

parts.note: a party is a person in a legal case

indicators.note: the rotten word goes round the exercise

parts.note: poor means bad or rotten
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: A litigant who is wretched at physical training spoils the fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dampens others' enjoyment is a killjoy, informal synonym.

clue.text: Seafood dish from Monkey Island

parts.note: a cheeky monkey is a scamp, a rascal

explanation.surface: A dish of seafood comes from Monkey Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded langoustine tails make a dish of seafood.

clue.text: Sportingly ignore the rain when actors are performing?

definitions.meaning: to continue a game despite the weather
when a play is on, actors are performing

explanation.surface: Players carry on through the rain while the actors perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Players carry on regardless; and a show that is being staged is on.

clue.text: See 12
Composed clue about cinema's altered view of Church unity

indicators.note: the reworked clue letters go round the other group
composed means put together, so the letters are rearranged
altered says the letters of cinema are changed in order

parts.note: the word cinema, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A clue is written about how a film house is changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' gives ECUL and 'altered' gives MENICA; the definition is a whole phrase describing an outlook, read as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecumenism promotes unity among Christian churches, so the adjective describes that outlook.

clue.text: Dull high school sort of lesson

parts.note: mat or matt means dull, without gloss

explanation.surface: A dull high-school class of some sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematics is a school subject, a kind of lesson.

clue.text: Portico ermine supplier shortened

indicators.note: shortened means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: the stoat's winter coat is ermine fur

explanation.surface: A porch is shortened by an ermine merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered colonnade in ancient Greece, a type of portico.

clue.text: Word with Cherry, say, at first sign of the Channel: "End of the line for Brummie?"

definitions.text: End of the line for Brummie?

parts.note: word means news, as in 'any word?'
a cherry is an example of a tree

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its initial letter

parts.note: a TV channel is a station

explanation.surface: Someone named Cherry gives news at the start of the channel, about a Birmingham railway terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brummie is someone from Birmingham, whose main railway terminus this is; Brummie is also this puzzle's setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Birmingham's chief railway terminus is where many lines end for a Birmingham traveller.

clue.text: Weller well before Davis?

parts.note: Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers
my! and well! are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Weller was healthy long before Davis arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the name that comes before Davis in Sammy Davis Jr, the American entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sammy Davis Jr was a famous American singer, so this first name precedes his surname.

clue.text: Sign of otic injury? Keep to one side!

definitions.meaning: otic means relating to the ear, so a blemish on that organ
to set aside for a particular purpose

explanation.surface: A doctor notes an ear wound and orders the patient to stay apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a mark on an ear; figuratively to reserve funds or items for a purpose.

clue.text: See 25
